US president Donald Trump has on Saturday criticised Spain over the migrant crisis in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, accusing Madrid of having “ZERO control” of its border.Trump also warned that the country could become “a ruined country” as political pressure mounts on prime minister Pedro Sánchez.“So sad what is happening in Spain, a country with ZERO control of its Border. WOW!” Trump said in a post on Truth Social on Saturday.His remarks follow a mass influx of migrants from Morocco into Ceuta, a small Spanish territory on North Africa’s coast, in July. Tens of thousands crossed by swimming, scaling fences or rushing through the border area, overwhelming local security forces.Trump had earlier criticised Spain’s handling of the crisis during an interview with British television channel GB News.“Spain will be a ruined country,” Trump said, describing the influx as an “invasion of a country”.“You know, you don't have thousands of people just bum-rushing your country. I've never seen anything like it,” he added.Trump also compared the situation with migration pressures facing Britain, saying the problem there was “not as visible as that (Ceuta)”.Spanish authorities said tens of thousands of people subsequently returned or were repatriated to Morocco, while thousands remained in Ceuta.Reports also raised questions over the role of Moroccan security forces in the border breach.Sánchez has rejected suggestions that Rabat helped orchestrate the crossing.“I can assure you that that no institution — neither the diplomatic service, nor the European Commission, nor any international body — has provided the Spanish government with solid evidence that Morocco planned or carried out the incident. None,” Sánchez told lawmakers on Thursday, according to the supplied report.The crisis has added to domestic pressure on Sánchez, with protests reported across Spain and calls for greater government action.The European Union has also yet to commit the assistance Spain has requested for Ceuta. EU Commission spokesperson Markus Lammert said Brussels was still assessing Madrid’s requests.“We're advancing on the assessment of these requests as a priority, however, for our final assessment, we have still some important open questions that need to be answered by the Spanish authorities first,” Lammert said.The dispute comes amid wider friction between Madrid and Washington over NATO spending and Spain’s refusal to endorse Trump’s proposed 5 per cent defence-spending target.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump has criticised Spain over the migrant crisis in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. He accused Madrid of having “ZERO control” of its border. Trump also warned that the country could become ‘a ruined country’ as political pressure mounts on prime minister Pedro Sánchez.

Article Title: ‘Something much bigger’: Trump planning major Middle East 'reset' after Iran war
Article Text:
According to a senior official, Trump has held two meetings in recent weeks to discuss the plan

The strategy

Regional alignment: Building an alliance among US allies in the Gulf to contain Iran, with Washington serving as a guarantor.

Building an alliance among US allies in the Gulf to contain Iran, with Washington serving as a guarantor. Addressing the October 7 fallout: Bringing the regional consequences of Hamas' October 7, 2023, attacks in israel closer to a conclusion by securing the next phase of Trump’s Gaza plan, reaching a security agreement between Israel and Syria, and implementing the Israel-Lebanon agreement.

Bringing the regional consequences of Hamas' October 7, 2023, attacks in israel closer to a conclusion by securing the next phase of Trump’s Gaza plan, reaching a security agreement between Israel and Syria, and implementing the Israel-Lebanon agreement. Expanding normalisation: Broadening the Abraham Accords and pursuing a normalisation agreement between Saudi Arabia and Israel.

Trump to push his post-war plan regardless of Israel election results?

US President Donald Trump is working on “something much bigger” for the Middle East once the Iran war ends, Axios reported, citing two US officials and other sources.“In recent weeks, the President has held two meetings with senior advisers to discuss the plan and raise ideas. In private conversations, he has said he is working on ‘something much bigger’ in the Middle East after the war with Iran,” the officials said."The initial work on the strategy is being carried out both at the senior political level of the Trump administration and at the working level across various government agencies," they added.As per the report, the initiative is part of a broader post-Iran war strategy being developed by the Trump administration. The plan seeks to contain Tehran’s regional influence while expanding efforts to normalise relations between Israel and its neighbours.The strategy remains in the early stages of drafting and is intended to shape Washington’s approach to the Middle East both after the Iran war and during the final two years of Trump’s ongoing second and final term in office.According to Axios, three main elements have been proposed as possible components of the strategy:However, two major events could affect the planning: Israel’s Knesset election in October and the US midterm elections in November.Of the two, the Israeli election is viewed as the more significant, particularly as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is currently trailing in pre-poll surveys.However, some US officials stressed that Trump would seek to implement his post-war strategy regardless of the outcome of Israel’s election, even if it results in a political stalemate.A source briefed on the process said it could take “another few weeks” to finalise the strategy.“They are cooking it, but it is not yet cooked. The idea is to tie a whole lot of things in the region together — how you create a regional alignment after the war. It is still unclear if all US allies in the region will be on board,” the source said.
Article Summary: The strategy is intended to shape Washington’s approach to the Middle East after the Iran war. It includes building an alliance among US allies in the Gulf to contain Iran, with Washington serving as a guarantor. It also includes reaching a security agreement between Israel and Syria, and implementing the Israel- Lebanon agreement.

Article Title: Hurricane Lowell holds Category 4 strength as Hawaii braces for a close call
Article Text:
This satellite image provided by CIRA/NOAA shows three storms, from left, Hurricane Lowell, Hurricane Karina and Tropical Storm Marie in the Pacific Ocean on Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. (CIRA/NOAA via AP)

Hawaii declares state of emergency

Lowell's track remains uncertain

Third storm to threaten Hawaii in weeks

Powerful Hurricane Lowell remained a Category 4 storm with winds of up to 150 mph on Saturday as Hawaii braced for potentially dangerous impacts from the system, which is expected to turn sharply northwards and pass close to the western islands early next week.The storm, currently more than 600 miles south of Hawaii, has fluctuated between Category 4 and Category 5 strength in recent days. Forecasters said some additional intensification was possible over the next day or so before Lowell begins to weaken, but it is expected to remain near Category 4 strength as it approaches the island chain.The greatest uncertainty is how close Lowell will come to Niihau and Kauai. The National Hurricane Center's current forecast puts the storm's centre about 150 miles west of Niihau and 190 miles west of Kauai on Tuesday morning. However, forecasters said confidence in the exact track remains lower than normal.A shift of less than 100 miles eastwards could bring the major hurricane much closer to Hawaii, potentially producing more direct and severe impacts. Forecast models currently show outcomes ranging from a devastating landfall on Kauai or Oahu to a track more than 400 miles west of Niihau, which would bring relatively limited effects.Even without a major shift in the track, dangerous conditions are expected. Rough seas, coastal flooding and strong rip currents could affect the islands from as early as this weekend, with the western islands facing the greatest risk.The National Weather Service warned that major coastal flooding is possible in Kauai, while significant coastal flooding could also affect Oahu. Lowell is expected to generate large waves and push additional water towards Hawaii's southern shores, while tides are also forecast to be near their highest levels of the month, increasing the potential for flooding.Hawaii Gov. Josh Green declared a state of emergency across the entire state on Thursday, allowing authorities to mobilise resources and activate Hawaii National Guard units.Six high-water vehicles are being deployed to Kauai, while Kauai County has begun clearing drainage systems and positioning equipment in areas vulnerable to flooding. At least two state parks on the island have also closed camping facilities ahead of the storm.State land and natural resources crews were due to notify campers on Friday that they must leave immediately, according to the county. Authorities have also urged residents to maintain 14 days' worth of supplies.“Our state is still recovering from Lala, and we are not waiting for another storm to get close before preparing,” Green said in a news release.Green warned that the state could face further tropical systems in the coming weeks, describing the current period as a serious storm season.“This is a serious storm season,” Green said at a news conference Friday, noting his state is likely to face additional threatening tropical systems in the coming weeks.“We’ve got multiple storms because of El Niño that are stacking up – we’re told that’s what the fall is going to be like,” the governor said.Lowell is forecast to turn sharply northwards this weekend after interacting with an area of low pressure high in the atmosphere north of Hawaii. The interaction is expected to pull the hurricane north, but the timing and strength of that interaction will determine how close the storm comes to the islands.Forecasters expect their confidence in Lowell's path to improve once the hurricane completes the turn.The storm's trajectory has drawn comparisons with Hurricane Iniki, which struck Kauai in 1992 as a Category 4 hurricane and remains Hawaii's worst storm on record.“We know that the memory of Hurricane ʻIniki is close to the surface for many of our families right now, so let us stay vigilant and prepare with a steady hand,” Kauai County Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami said in a statement.He urged residents to remain patient, take care on the roads and check on their neighbours.“We don’t need any unforeseen tragedies while everyone is preparing,” Kawakami said. “Also, use this time to prepare and talk story with your ʻohana tonight so everyone knows the plan.”On Oahu, officials have also urged residents to remain vigilant, although the current forecast suggests the island's capital and largest city faces less immediate risk.“We feel much better about where things stand for Oʻahu heading into this weekend, but we are going to stay vigilant until Lowell makes that turn and moves away from us,” Honolulu Mayor Rick Blangiardi said in a statement.Lowell is the third tropical system to threaten Hawaii in roughly three weeks. Hurricane Lala brought feet of rain to the Big Island in mid-August, triggering severe flooding and causing extensive damage in communities along the island's southern end.Tropical Storm Moke followed later in August. Although it brought rain to the Big Island, its weaker strength meant the impacts were considerably less severe.The succession of storms has raised concerns as El Niño strengthens activity across the Pacific hurricane season. For Hawaii, the immediate focus remains on Lowell and the uncertainty surrounding its eventual path.“We’re hopeful that it will miss us, but if it does what Iniki did in 1992 or even does anything close … we could see tragic consequences,” Green said.
Article Summary: Lowell is forecast to turn sharply northwards this weekend after interacting with an area of low pressure high in the atmosphere north of Hawaii. The interaction is expected to pull the hurricane north, but the timing and strength of that interaction will determine how close the storm comes to the islands. Rough seas, coastal flooding and strong rip currents could affect the islands from as early as this weekend.

Article Title: 'Highly useful' but no breakthrough: What was discussed in Putin-US talks on Ukraine
Article Text:
President Vladimir Putin, background center left, speaks to U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff, center foreground, back to a camera, and Jared Kushner, right, as Kremlin foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov, second left, and Presidential Envoy Kirill Dmitriev attend the talks at the Senate Palace of the Kremlin in Moscow, on Saturday

What was discussed?

Russian President Vladimir Putin’s three-hour meeting with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow ended without any reported breakthrough on a Ukraine peace deal, even as the Kremlin described the talks as “highly useful” and said discussions would continue.Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the meeting, which lasted three hours and 10 minutes, was substantive, constructive and extremely frank and took place in a trusting atmosphere, according to Russia’s TASS news agency.The US envoys “outlined a number of ideas regarding possible avenues for a settlement”, Ushakov said. He did not disclose the details of those proposals, leaving unclear whether they addressed the most contentious issues between Moscow and Kyiv, including territory and the future security arrangements for Ukraine.Ushakov said Putin presented Moscow’s assessment of the war and stressed Russia’s battlefield gains.“In particular, note was taken of the real advances made by the Russian army within the combat zone; confidence was expressed in achieving the stated objectives, and the need to eliminate all root causes of the conflict was emphasised,” he said, according to ANI.Putin also reiterated Moscow’s willingness to pursue political and diplomatic solutions with Washington.The Kremlin has repeatedly said any settlement must address what it calls the “root causes” of the conflict.The discussions also moved beyond the war. “The talks went beyond a mere exchange of views on resolving the Ukrainian crisis. Economic issues and potential major, mutually beneficial Russian-American projects were discussed in some detail,” Ushakov said, according to Reuters.“Overall, one can say that the negotiations were timely and highly useful for both sides,” he added.Putin also praised US President Donald Trump’s efforts to end the war.“Understanding that he is entering a difficult situation, he nevertheless does not stop his efforts to help bring about a settlement and to make his contribution to resolving the Russian-Ukrainian conflict,” Putin said in a televised remarks at the start of the talks..A White House official told Reuters the talks were “substantive” and that next steps would be announced in the coming weeks.The US envoys were due to travel to Kyiv on Sunday for talks with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy. Ushakov said they would convey Putin’s observations on prospects for a “durable peaceful settlement”, while Moscow and Washington would maintain further contact through the envoys.Despite the positive language from Moscow, the central disputes remain unresolved, leaving the next round of US contacts with Kyiv crucial to determining whether the latest diplomatic push can narrow the gap between the two sides.
Article Summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow. The three-hour meeting ended without any reported breakthrough on a Ukraine peace deal. Kremlin described the talks as “highly useful” and said discussions would continue.

Article Title: Scientists discover nearly 1 billion tons of water locked inside Utah's rocky glaciers, using gravity measurements to map ice buried beneath mountain debris
Article Text:
Image: AI Generated

A glacier hidden beneath rocks

Scientists used gravity to see underground ice

Images of Timpanogos Rock Glacier. (a) Photo of Timpanogos Rock Glacier on 1 August 1925, showing the rock glacier (right side of the frame) flanked by seasonal snow (University of Utah Photo Archives)(b) Image of a moulin-like feature on the upper portion of Timpanogos Rock Glacier, with layers of firn separated by thin debris layers. We expect that the firn transitions to ice at depth. (Image: University of Utah Photo Archives)

One Utah rock glacier holds hundreds of swimming pools of water

A hidden water reserve facing a changing climate

At first glance, Utah's rocky mountain slopes may look completely dry, with loose stones and boulders covering the ground. But beneath some of those rocks lies an enormous store of frozen water. Researchers have now estimated that Utah's rock glaciers contain about 0.99 gigatonnes, or nearly 1 billion tons, of water equivalent. These unusual formations are bodies of ice buried beneath thick layers of rock and debris, allowing them to survive in places where conventional glaciers cannot. The discovery comes from a study of the Timpanogos Rock Glacier beneath Mount Timpanogos, where scientists used subtle changes in Earth's gravitational field to reconstruct what was hidden underground. Published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Earth Surface, the research was led by Bronson Cvijanovich with Michael S. Thorne, Surya Pachhai, Leif S. Anderson, Ivan Tochimani-Hernandez, Christian L. Hardwick and Tonie van Dam, from the University of Utah and Utah Geological Survey.Rock glaciers look nothing like the bright, exposed ice fields people normally associate with glaciers. They are instead masses of ice covered by layers of loose rocks and debris, with the ice slowly moving downhill beneath the surface.That rocky blanket can insulate the ice from warmth and sunlight, allowing these formations to persist in mountain environments that may no longer support conventional glaciers. The researchers explain in their study, ‘ The Internal Ice Content of Timpanogos Rock Glacier, Utah, USA From 3-D Bayesian Inversion of Gravity Data, ’ that rock glaciers are increasingly important as climate change reduces conventional glacier ice. They can store water, provide refuges for cold-adapted species and, if destabilised, create hazards for communities below. Yet scientists have struggled to determine exactly how much ice these formations contain because their rocky surfaces hide their interiors.To look beneath Timpanogos Rock Glacier, the team turned to a method that does not require drilling through the entire formation. They collected 232 gravity measurements across the site and used a three-dimensional Bayesian inversion to reconstruct the hidden structure. Ice is substantially less dense than the surrounding bedrock, so a sufficiently large buried ice mass creates a tiny but measurable reduction in gravitational acceleration. By mapping these variations, researchers could estimate where the ice-rich material was located and how thick it was. The study also found an estimated ice volume of about 1.55 million cubic metres, with an average thickness of 18.8 metres. The researchers' preferred model indicates that the entire rock glacier is about 72% ice by volume, while its ice core is approximately 83% ice.The amount of ice beneath Mount Timpanogos is difficult to visualise, so the researchers compared it with something more familiar. Their estimated 1.55 million cubic metres of ice is roughly equivalent to the volume of 600 Olympic-sized swimming pools. More importantly, Timpanogos Rock Glacier provided the researchers with a way to estimate the hidden water stored across many similar formations. Using their measurements alongside data from other rock glaciers, the team developed a new area-volume relationship. In the research this method produced an estimate of 0.99 gigatonnes of water equivalent for Utah's intact rock glaciers. The western United States was estimated to contain about 11.92 gigatonnes, while intact rock glaciers worldwide could hold approximately 48.03 gigatonnes.The discovery matters because rock glaciers could become increasingly important as conventional glaciers retreat. Their insulating debris can protect buried ice for longer, making them relatively resilient stores of frozen water in warming mountain environments. But the researchers also caution that their estimates are not perfectly complete. Persistent snow and steep terrain prevented gravity measurements in the upper reaches of Timpanogos Rock Glacier, meaning the calculated ice volume is likely a lower estimate of the total. The study also notes uncertainties in modelling the relationship between ice thickness and density. Even so, the findings reveal a substantial reservoir that is almost invisible from the surface. As temperatures rise and mountain ice changes, understanding these buried stores could become increasingly important for water resources, ecosystems and assessing hazards in alpine regions.
Article Summary: Scientists used gravity to see underground ice beneath Utah's Timpanogos Rock Glacier. They estimated that Utah's rock glaciers contain about 0.99 gigatonnes, or nearly 1 billion tons, of water equivalent. Discovery matters because rock glaciers could become increasingly important as climate change reduces conventional glacier ice.

Article Title: Two dead, two critical after small plane crashes in California
Article Text:
2 dead, 2 injured in California plane crash

Two people were killed and two others critically injured after a small plane crashed near Sierra Sky Park Airport in Fresno, California, in the US, on Saturday.The aircraft crashed near Blythe Avenue, close to Sierra Sky Park Airport, according to ABC30 News, which cited the Fresno fire department. The circumstances leading to the crash were not immediately clear.The two injured were taken to hospital in critical condition, the department said.Several agencies responded to the crash site, including the Fresno police department, Fresno fire department, Fresno County sheriff’s office and North Central fire department, ABC30 News reported. Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) also responded after the incident affected power supplies in the surrounding area.According to PG&E’s outage map, electricity was briefly disrupted for nearby residents following the crash. The outage was later restored. The US authorities have not yet released further details about the identities of those involved or what caused the aircraft to crash. The incident remains under investigation.
Article Summary: Small plane crashes near Sierra Sky Park Airport in Fresno, California, on Saturday. Two people killed and two others critically injured, fire department said. The circumstances leading to the crash were not immediately clear. Power supplies in the area were briefly disrupted, but later restored.

Article Title: No room to be kind: US immigration judges told to reduce time for people awaiting Green Card before being deported
Article Text:
At a mandatory training, US judges were told to reduce time given to people awaiting visas or green cards before being deported.

A Guardian report claimed that immigration judges across the US have been asked to be strict and deny people time as they wait for their Green Cards so that they can be deported. A mandatory training for judges also urged them to threaten attorneys who accept too many immigration cases. “There is no room to be kind; there is only urgency to make them leave [the US], one way or the other," the judges were told.Citing sources, the Guardian report claimed that hundreds of immigration judges attended a mandatory presentation in recent days about “continuances” – a legal tool which has historically been used to give immigrants more time to find lawyers, build their cases or wait for approval of their applications for documents at another federal immigration agency.The virtual training session was led by a veteran immigration judge, Keith Hunsucker, of the Board of immigration appeals, the immigration courts’ appellate branch. He denied over 80% of asylum cases for much of the time that he was on the bench in immigration court before moving on to other roles, the report said.The training was apparently meant to reduce the immigration court backlog and they were taught that some continuances are sought solely for the purpose of delay and persons illegally present in the United States who wish to remain have a substantial incentive to prolong litigation so they may avoid deportation as long as possible.Continuance requests solely for dilatory purposes should not be countenanced by Immigration Judges,” one slide readAn approved visa petition should not delay deportation proceedings if the visa itself is not yet available because of annual quotas but would be issued to the qualified recipient at a later, albeit unspecified, date, the training suggested.Though there is a huge backlog, the judges were told during the training that immigration attorneys risk punitive measures for accepting what are deemed too many cases. “Where a practitioner takes on more cases than he or she can responsibly and professionally handle,” one of the slides read, “it may be appropriate for an Immigration Judge to consider referral to EOIR disciplinary counsel for further action and possible sanction for a violation. ”
Article Summary: A Guardian report claims that immigration judges have been asked to be strict and deny people time as they wait for their Green Cards so that they can be deported. A mandatory training for judges also urged them to threaten attorneys who accept too many immigration cases. “There is no room to be kind; there is only urgency to make them leave [the US], one way or the other," the judges were told.

Article Title: ‘Growing differences between military, Asif Zardari’: Self-exiled Pakistani politician Altaf Hussain makes big claim
Article Text:
Self-exiled British-Pakistani politician Altaf Hussain (File photo)

Self-exiled British-Pakistani politician Altaf Hussain has alleged a "silent struggle" is underway between Pakistan's powerful military establishment and President Asif Ali Zardari , warning that a debate over creating new provinces could push the country into a major political and security crisis.The founder of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM) claimed that discussions were underway on a possible 28th Constitutional Amendment, which could include provisions for the creation of new provinces.“Discussions on the creation of new provinces have been raised by interior minister Mohsin Naqvi and DG-ISPR. The proposed constitutional changes reflect growing differences between President Asif Ali Zardari and the military leadership. A political deadlock could lead to serious constitutional consequences, including the imposition of martial law or the formation of an interim government,” Hussain said in a TikTok message on September 2.Referring to the earlier 26th and 27th Amendments, he alleged that political parties had previously reached agreements to facilitate their passage.Hussain also questioned the prolonged foreign stay of Zardari, the husband of slain former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and father of ex-foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari."The President had travelled to Austria in connection for his son Bilawal Zardari’s wedding and is currently in London. There was also an hour-long meeting between Zardari and Naqvi in London, claiming that an important message was conveyed to the President," he added.Hussain further cautioned that tensions between the Pakistan military and Sindhi nationalist groups could escalate into widespread unrest. Referring to the situation in Balochistan, Hussain said violence between security forces and Baloch fighters was continuing and called for greater political consideration for the Baloch people.He warned that if Pakistan descended into a broader civil conflict, foreign powers, including the US and UK, would not come to its rescue, and urged Pakistanis to heed his warnings.
Article Summary: Self-exiled British-Pakistani politician Altaf Hussain has alleged a "silent struggle" is underway between Pakistan's powerful military establishment and President Asif Ali Zardari. The founder of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM) claimed that discussions were underway on a possible 28th Constitutional Amendment.

Article Title: 25 Pakistani military personnel killed in Balochistan attacks, BLA claims
Article Text:
Balochistan: BLA claims 25 Pakistani military personnel killed in two attacks (Picture from X)

The Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) on Thursday claimed responsibility for two attacks in Pakistan’s Balochistan province, saying 25 Pakistani military personnel were killed and three military vehicles destroyed.According to The Balochistan Post, the BLA spokesperson said fighters targeted a military convoy at Ziarat Cross, attacking vehicles and destroying two of them, including a military truck.The militant group initially claimed that 18 personnel were killed in the attack, with the death toll later rising to 25.The BLA also released a one-minute-and-11-second video trailer through Hakkal, its official media channel, which it said showed footage from the Ziarat Cross attack.The footage purportedly shows armed fighters near burning Pakistani military vehicles, with bodies visible at the site and weapons being seized. The BLA said it would release the complete video later.In a separate operation in the Hajika area of Surab, the group’s Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) remotely detonated an explosives-laden vehicle, destroying a military vehicle and killing seven personnel, according to the BLA statement.
Article Summary: Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) claims responsibility for two attacks in Pakistan's Balochistan province. BLA says 25 Pakistani military personnel were killed and three military vehicles destroyed. The militant group also released a one-minute-and-11-second video trailer through Hakkal.

Article Title: ‘6ft by 8ft cell, brown drinking water’: What Imran Khan’s jail cell is like
Article Text:
The report said visitors have been barred and Khan has been confined to his cell for as much as 23 hours a day.

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan is being held in what has been described as harsh conditions at Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail, with reports alleging prolonged isolation, limited access to reading material and restrictions on contact with his family.According to a report by The Times UK, Khan is being kept in a 6ft by 8ft cell typically used for prisoners on death row. The report said the 73-year-old has no reading material apart from the Quran and is being provided “soiled brown water” to drink.His sons, Sulaiman and Kasim Khan, have reportedly been unable to meet their father in person since 2022 and have at times been prevented from speaking to him by telephone for months. They have described his living conditions as inhumane “torture tactics”.The report said visitors have been barred and Khan has been confined to his cell for as much as 23 hours a day.The reported restrictions have also become the subject of repeated legal challenges by Khan’s family.His sister Uzma Khan filed a fresh contempt petition in the Supreme Court on Wednesday, alleging that authorities have failed to comply with an August 18 order concerning Khan’s access to his family.According to The Express Tribune, the petition names Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Adiala Jail Superintendent Sajid Baig, Punjab Inspector General of Prisons Mian Salik Jalal and other senior officials as respondents.The August 18 order had directed authorities to facilitate virtual communication between Khan and his sons and allow his sisters to meet him weekly. However, Uzma said she was denied a scheduled visit on Tuesday, while telephone communication between Khan and his sons has remained restricted since March.The petition also alleges that authorities failed to establish the infrastructure required for bi-weekly telephone calls with Sulaiman and Kasim.The latest dispute follows an earlier contempt petition over the alleged non-compliance with the Supreme Court’s direction to transfer Khan to Shifa International Hospital for medical evaluation. He was instead taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) on August 21 before being returned to Adiala Jail after doctors declared him “medically fit”. Authorities have cited security concerns for the decision.
Article Summary: Imran Khan is being held in what has been described as harsh conditions at Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail. Reports allege prolonged isolation, limited access to reading material and restrictions on contact with his family. His sons, Sulaiman and Kasim Khan, have reportedly been unable to meet their father in person since 2022.

Article Title: Pakistan: Imran Khan's sister files fresh contempt plea over denied jail visits
Article Text: Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan's sister Uzma Khan on Wednesday filed a fresh contempt of court petition in the Supreme Court, alleging non-enforcement of previous judicial directives issued by the country's apex court.In her petition, Uzma named several high-ranking officials, including Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif and Adiala (Rawalpindi Central Jail) Superintendent Sajid Baig, as respondents.According to the Express Tribune, the petition was filed after the Supreme Court's August 18 instructions, which mandated virtual communication between Imran Khan and his sons, alongside weekly access for his sisters, failed to materialise.The plea said that Uzma Khan was denied a scheduled visit on Tuesday and noted that audio communication with his sons has remained restricted since March.The petition alleged that authorities neglected to establish the necessary infrastructure enabling bi-weekly telephone calls with his sons, Kasim Khan and Sulaiman Khan, as previously ordered by the bench.Earlier, Uzma had filed another contempt application addressing government non-compliance regarding a separate instruction within the August 18 order, which directed that Imran Khan be moved to Shifa International Hospital for medical care.Under the original August 18 decision, the Supreme Court instructed that the former premier be transferred to Shifa International Hospital for clinical evaluation by a multidisciplinary medical panel while simultaneously granting visitation rights.Following the orders, authorities transferred Imran Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) on August 21. He was, however, sent back to Adiala Jail shortly after medical personnel declared him to be "medically fit".Reacting to the developments, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) lambasted prison administrators for barring relatives from seeing the party founder, characterising the restrictions as a flagrant breach of mandates issued by both the Supreme Court and the Islamabad High Court, as reported by another Pakistan-based daily, Dawn.
Article Summary: Imran Khan's sister Uzma Khan has filed a contempt of court petition in the Supreme Court. She alleges non-enforcement of previous judicial directives issued by the country's apex court. Uzma named several high-ranking officials, including Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif and Adiala (Rawalpindi Central Jail) Superintendent Sajid Baig as respondents.

Article Title: Pak pleads for dialogue after India stands firm on suspending Indus Water Treaty
Article Text:
Indus Waters treaty representational image

India rejects tribunal ruling

Water, terrorism and the SCO

NEW DELHI: Just days after India rejected an international tribunal's ruling on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) and dismissed its jurisdiction, Pakistan on Wednesday urged New Delhi to engage "constructively" within the framework of the 1960 water-sharing agreement.According to news agency PTI, Pakistan foreign office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said the Permanent Court of Arbitration had reaffirmed that the treaty remained fully enforced and binding. Pakistan, he said, would take “all possible measures” to ensure the decision was implemented.Andrabi said Pakistan remained committed to implementing the treaty in letter and spirit in accordance with its language and provisions.Pakistan will continue to urge India to reciprocate with the same approach whereby the treaty is upheld in letter and spirit and in its full legal documented provisions, he said, according to PTI.Pakistan had approached the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague in March 2026, seeking a determination on the status of the treaty after India placed it in abeyance.India, however, has consistently rejected the jurisdiction of the arbitration process.On Monday, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said, “India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body.”“India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance remains in force,” the ministry said.MEA said the Court of Arbitration had issued what it termed an award on May 15, 2026, concerning maximum pondage supplemental to an earlier award on issues of general interpretation of the IWT."This so-called Court was constituted by the World Bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty and India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body", the ministry stated.India has maintained that the establishment of the arbitral body itself violates the IWT and that it has no jurisdiction over India’s sovereign decision to place the treaty in abeyance.The dispute also featured indirectly at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, in Bishkek, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for action against countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy.“We cannot remain confined to an action-reaction approach,” Modi said, calling for the dismantling of terrorist ecosystems, including funding networks, recruitment pipelines and territorial sanctuaries.Pakistan prime minister Shehbaz Sharif, speaking at the summit, described water as the region’s “lifeblood” and said it “must never be weaponised”.“The treaties governing our shared waters are solemn, binding international commitments. They are not matters of political convenience to be cast aside at your will. They must be honoured unconditionally, in both letter and spirit,” Sharif said, according to Dawn.India placed the IWT in abeyance following the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed. The Cabinet Committee on Security took the decision on April 23, 2025, with New Delhi saying the conditions underlying the treaty had fundamentally changed.India has said the treaty will remain in abeyance until Pakistan “credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism”.
Article Summary: Pakistan urges New Delhi to engage "constructively" within the framework of the 1960 water-sharing agreement. Pakistan had approached the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague in March 2026, seeking a determination on the status of the treaty. India, however, has consistently rejected the jurisdiction of the arbitration process.

Article Title: Leadership gaps cloud Pakistan's human rights oversight system
Article Text:
Pakistan human rights faces pending vacancy

NCHR’s legal status under question

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is most important for an effective human rights body? Strong leadership Independence Transparency Accountability 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s human rights oversight framework is facing growing uncertainty as key commissions continue to function without permanent leadership or full membership, raising concerns over their independence and effectiveness.The previous National Commission for Human Rights (NCHR) completed its four-year term in November 2025, but a new commission has yet to be fully constituted, news agency ANI cited in its report. The National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW) is also functioning under an acting chairperson.Former NCHR chairperson Khawar Mumtaz criticised and warned that prolonged reliance on temporary arrangements could weaken the autonomy and performance of independent rights bodies.Human rights activist Peter Jacob said Parliament passed legislation establishing the National Commission for Minorities Rights in December 2025, but appointments to the body remain incomplete.The National Commission on the Rights of the Child has also faced vacancies. The Ministry of Human Rights invited applications in July 2026 for members representing Punjab, Islamabad and Balochistan, The Express Tribune reported.An amendment to the National Commission for Human Rights Act in 2026 introduced Section 4A, allowing a chairperson to continue for up to 120 days after the expiry of their term or until a successor is appointed.NCHR Chairperson Rabiya Javeri Agha maintained that the commission remains operationally effective, pointing to additional staff recruited two years ago. She said the extension of the chairperson’s tenure was made under the law and reflected practices followed by human rights institutions internationally. Questions regarding the constitution of a new commission, she said, should be directed to the government, according to The Express Tribune.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s human rights oversight framework is facing growing uncertainty. Key commissions continue to function without permanent leadership or full membership. Article Title: Imran Khan, wife Bushra Bibi get slight relief as Pak HC bars solitary confinement
Article Text:
Pak HC intervenes over Imran Khan, wife Bushra Bibi's detention, bars solitary confinement

A Pakistan high court on Tuesday directed authorities at Rawalpindi Jail to ensure that former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi are not held in solitary confinement. The ruling also set out provisions for Khan's family meetings, phone calls, reading material and medical care.The Islamabad High Court (IHC), while hearing petitions challenging the couple's alleged solitary confinement, directed the jail authorities to allow Khan's family members to meet him in line with prison rules and arrange telephone conversations with his sons.Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro also ordered the jail to provide Khan with newspapers and books every day and ensure access to medical facilities as prescribed under jail rules. Rawalpindi's Aiala jail superintendent has been asked to implement the directions and submit a compliance report within 15 days, according to the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).The court had earlier reserved its verdict on August 6 on separate petitions filed by Khan's sister Aleema Khanum and Bushra Bibi's daughter Mubashra Khawar Maneka. The IHC also held the petitions challenging the alleged solitary confinement to be maintainable.The 73-year-old cricketer-turned-politician and his wife have been in custody since August 2023 and is serving prison terms in corruption and related cases. Khan's Tehreek-e-Insaf party and supporters have maintained that the cases are politically motivated, while the government has rejected allegations of mistreatment.Bushra Bibi was first jailed in January 2024 after being convicted in a corruption-related case. She was released on bail in October that year after nearly nine months in custody but was arrested again in January 2025 following another corruption conviction. She remains at Adiala Jail.The IHC order comes as Khan's detention and medical treatment remain the subject of separate proceedings before the Supreme Court.On Monday, the Supreme Court declined an application by Khan's sister Uzma Khan seeking an early hearing of her contempt petition against government officials over the alleged failure to comply with an earlier order concerning his transfer to a private hospital, Dawn reported.Pakistan's Supreme Court had on August 18 ordered that Khan be shifted to the privately run Shifa International Hospital after concerns were raised by his family and supporters over his health, including an eye condition diagnosed earlier this year.Instead, Khan was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) on the night of August 20-21 for a medical procedure and diagnostic examinations and was later returned to Adiala Jail.Uzma Khan's petition contends that this breached the Supreme Court's direction that Khan remain admitted at the Islamabad hospital until the next hearing on September 16. The government has defended the decision, citing security concerns.Two specialists from Shifa International Hospital also participated in Khan's eye examination at PIMS, according to the hospital administration, as reported by Dawn.Uzma Khan had sought an earlier hearing, arguing that further delay could affect the enforcement of the Supreme Court's order. The Supreme Court, however, rejected the request under its case-fixation policy, noting that 94 other criminal original petitions in the same category were pending, Dawn reported.The contempt petition is listed for September 16 before a three-member bench comprising Justices Shahid Waheed, Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibrahim. The bench is also scheduled to hear other matters concerning Khan's health and family meetings.
Article Summary: Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi have been in custody since August 2023. The couple is serving prison terms in corruption and related cases. The Islamabad High Court ordered the jail authorities to allow Khan's family members to meet him in line with prison rules.

Article Title: Pakistan power crisis deepens as Karachi reels from 24-hour blackouts

​Karachi reels under deepening power crisis as blackouts last up to 24 hours

Karachi's electricity crisis has intensified, with residents in several parts of the city reporting outages lasting up to 24 hours. Rights activists in Pakistan have warned that prolonged loadshedding is placing a growing burden on low-income families.According to Dawn, the issue was raised at a press conference at the Karachi Press Club organised by the Civil Society Collective for Clean Energy for Karachi. Speakers said extended power cuts were disrupting basic household activities, education and work, while also worsening access to water and affecting hygiene.Residents of North Karachi, Nazimabad and parts of Gulistan-i-Jauhar reported between 16 and 24 hours of loadshedding, ANI said. Protests and traffic disruptions were also reported in Lyari and other parts of the old city during the week beginning August 24.The speakers cited K-Electric's published outage schedule, saying more than 615 feeders were listed for power cuts of up to 12 hours a day. Article Title: Pakistan court allows Hindu woman to return home after alleged forced conversion, marriage
Article Text:
Woman returns from Pakistan

'Want to return home'

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that the court made the right decision in allowing Reeta to return to her parents? Yes, it was the right decision. A court in Pakistan on Tuesday allowed a 21-year-old Hindu woman to return to her parents after she told the magistrate that she wished to go home of her own free will, days after her family alleged that she had been abducted and pressured to convert to Islam and marry a Muslim man, news agency PTI reported.Shirimati Reeta, a resident of Rana Rajput Colony in Khipro tehsil of Sindh’s Sanghar district, went missing from her hometown last week, according to a complaint filed by her brother Ravi Shankar. He alleged that CCTV footage showed unidentified people taking Reeta from the family home along with valuables and mobile phones on August 24.According to the complaint, Reeta was taken to Gujranwala in Punjab, some 80 kms from Lahore, where she was allegedly pressured to convert to Islam and marry Nazeer Hussain, who was already married.Punjab Police later recovered Reeta and produced her before a judicial magistrate on Monday. The investigating officer sought to place her in Darul Aman, a state-run shelter, claiming that she was unwilling to return to her parents.Her lawyers, Asad Jamal and Kheta Ram, opposed the request and told the court that Reeta wanted to return home with her brother, who was present in court, a court official said.The magistrate then asked Reeta to record her statement under oath. “In her statement, Reeta said that she wanted to return to her parents’ home of her own free will,” the official said.The court subsequently allowed Reeta to leave with her brother and made him responsible for her safe custody and transportation back to the family home in Sanghar.
Article Summary: Shirimati Reeta, a 21-year-old Hindu woman, went missing from her hometown last week. Her family alleged that she had been abducted and pressured to convert to Islam and marry a Muslim man. Police later recovered Reeta and produced her before a judicial magistrate on Monday. Article Title: Watch: 'Driverless' car crashes into police van after internet outage in Islamabad
Article Text:
In a social media post on Monday, Aalijah sought to clarify that his video was not intended to ridicule Zafar or undermine his work and warned that the technology was not yet ready to be considered completely reliable.

A remotely operated driverless car crashed into a police van in Islamabad after losing its internet connection during a demonstration, with footage of the incident going viral and sparking a wave of memes online.According to local media, the incident took place at D-Chowk, a high-security area in the Pakistani capital, where journalist Muhammad Aalijah was recording a video of a technology-based automated-driving system developed by Abbottabad-based technology enthusiast Ehsan Zafar. The car was being controlled remotely over the internet when a sudden connectivity failure caused its steering to malfunction.Footage shared by Aalijah shows him sitting in the front passenger seat as he explains the vehicle's features while it moves along the road. The remotely controlled steering wheel then appears to lose control, sending the car towards a police van parked nearby.Aalijah can be seen attempting to stop the vehicle by pulling the handbrake, but the car continues moving and bumps into the police vehicle.Aalijah later told Dawn that he had been asked by Zafar to report on his technology-based automated-driving innovation. He attributed the crash to a "technical fault" triggered by an internet disruption.“Everything was fine until a technical fault occurred due to an internet disruption, causing the car to go out of control and crash into a police vehicle,” he said.According to Aalijah, the vehicle was operated remotely through internet and satellite connections. The loss of the internet connection during the demonstration caused the car to become uncontrollable.In a social media post on Monday, Aalijah sought to clarify that his video was not intended to ridicule Zafar or undermine his work.“The sole purpose was to raise awareness and urge people to remain cautious until any new experiment or technology has been thoroughly tested, proven safe and established as a complete success,” he said.“This was a message of caution, not an attempt to discredit anyone.”Aalijah also warned that the technology was not yet ready to be considered completely reliable.“The vehicle was being operated through satellite and internet connections, but during external control, it went out of control as soon as the internet connection was disconnected and collided with a police vehicle,” he wrote.He said the relatively low traffic at D-Chowk limited the potential consequences of the malfunction, but warned that a similar failure on a busy road could have been far more serious.“If the same situation had occurred on a busy road, the consequences could have been extremely dangerous, even fatal,” he said.“This video is not criticism; it is a responsible effort to raise awareness and issue a warning by all means, experiment, but ensure safety first,” he added.
Article Summary: A remotely operated driverless car crashed into a police van in Islamabad after losing its internet connection during a demonstration. The incident took place at D-Chowk, a high-security area in the Pakistani capital. The car was being controlled remotely over the internet when a sudden connectivity failure caused its steering to malfunction. Footage of the incident went viral and sparked a wave of memes online.

Article Title: Pak PM scrambles for damage control after his office edits leaders out of SCO summit photo

The edited framing keeps Sharif at the centre alongside several prominent leaders

What’s was on the agenda

What

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif appeared to go into damage-control mode on Tuesday after his office shared an edited version of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit’s family photograph, cropping out several world leaders while keeping Sharif prominently at the centre of the frame.The Pakistan Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) first shared the edited summit photograph at 11:42am IST.The full image showed the heads of SCO member states and senior officials standing together ahead of a session of the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek.From left, the photograph featured SCO Secretary-General Nurlan Yermekbayev, Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Chinese Minister shared the full family photograph featuring all the world leaders.The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Leadership Summit focused on strengthening regional cooperation and addressing shared security, economic and geopolitical challenges.The summit, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary was held in the expanded “SCO Plus” format, bringing together leaders from member,
